# Independent audit of three actual-fiber constructions


None of them is a general OC proof.

## Common-normal allocation hulls

Source: `candidate 8a1fb011e3d0549f`.

The inclusion uses strict allocations larger than an actual deficient
cap's three captured volumes. Each ordinary depth region then lies
strictly outside its own cut, and the affine relation of the three
thresholds keeps the endpoint midpoint set outside the same middle
cut. Compactness preserves strict separation after the convex hull.
Empty regions and the purely integer halfspace case are explicitly
handled. Every candidate lies in the actual middle fiber.

The nesting argument in the level r and the inclusion of the separated
ordinary-core certificates are valid. The interval example checks all
real allocations by exhaustive status cases; its reverse singleton
bounds use epsilon families only to bound a fixed candidate. The exact
endpoint tail calculation gives the claimed strict pointwise gain.

The two-allocation simplex obstruction is conclusive even for the FULL
ordinary depth fields, not only the proposed homothetic inner cores.
Its second allocation sums to the target, its A depth region is empty,
and the opposite coordinate-sum cut separates every point of the first
allocation's midpoint simplex from the second K depth region. Thus
universal nonemptiness is false. the contributor reran the exact verifier PASS.

## Joint critical-cap profiles

Source: `candidate 0354c832e0d018af`.

The ordinary distal trimming proof retains a convex positive-volume
body when the asserted inequality is nontrivial, and applies ordinary
Grunbaum to a covering original cap at that retained body's centroid.
No mixed-measure version is invoked. The two profile thresholds sum to
Q, and the resulting positive-part identity is exactly the distance
from tau to [q_i,q_i+V_i]. Actual cap indices and cross-captures stay
coupled throughout. The three-cap median expression and ties are correct.

For two caps the signs of the covered overlap and uncovered gap follow
from the two actual interval thresholds in each endpoint fiber. The
bound Q> M/4 under strict noheavy is sufficient for Gamma_d M/2,
including the separate Gamma_1=1/2 endpoint of that comparison.

The centroid assertions are conditional on a below-target actual
critical budget. Strict noheavy makes every pair of whole-fiber masses
exceed M/2, excluding double-centroid incidence. The coarea bound divides
section area by ||u||, correctly matching functional rather than metric
thickness. The signed drift cancels in the summed endpoint charges;
none of these equations supplies a common improving direction.
The explicit padded-interval example's centroid margin table confirms
that automatic double-centroid matching is genuinely false.

## Signed centroid-shell compensation

Source: `candidate d4b54fbaf58fa904`.

The nested actual body has exactly T,rT,T as its integer fibers. Its
projected density and shell first moment give the stated cap difference
(1-3Gamma_d)Delta and the opposite difference 3Gamma_d Delta. The
sign uses Gamma_d>1/3, and the condition rc<=1 is necessary and retained.
These directional statements are not called a global depth comparison.

The separate planar product-depth proof treats all projected triangle
vertex-value parameters, both reflection regimes, all integer tilts,
and pure integer caps. Its quadratic paired-tail minimum and endpoint
limits verify the raw product depth 4|T|/3. At r=141/100, the displayed
oblique cap through the moving centroid has exactly the three stated
volumes and is smaller by97|T|/30000. Strict noheavy and membership of
that centroid in the original T are verified. The old centroid remains
a better actual point by nested-set monotonicity. Hence this is a
counterexample to centroid-path compensation, not to OC or to monotonic
global raw depth under adding measure. the contributor reran the1310 exact checks.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
